pr_body:
# Objective

Make it clear when a trait is being used for its extension methods, not for itself.
Fixes #16268 
Fixes #13959

## Solution

Use `as _` for obvious cases.

## Testing

Code compiles
pr_comments:
> I do wish there was a lint though.

@alice-i-cecile If you mean a lint for being told when you could apply `as _` on a trait that is only used anonymously, there's the [`clippy::unused-trait-names`](https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/index.html#unused_trait_names) lint.
Oh, is that not enabled? I'll check that.

This should be in-line with the lint and show the fullness of it. It's just a question of whether we like this or not. If we don't like it, then let's close those issues and maybe remove the existing instances of `as _`. Personally, I do like it. We run commands like `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --fix` anyway. This is automatically handled as part of the existing dev workflow and the concerns mentioned thus far only have to do with typing and maintaining the imports themselves. In other words, we don't need r-a to do this automatically because we already run clippy regularly.

issue_context.title: Using `trait as _` to avoid namespace pollution
issue_context.body:
> This is really interesting, I hadn't considered using `trait as _` to avoid name collisions. At a glance this also works in [preludes](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2021&gist=2d58697888b02fc3ff00a4ecb0234e2f). For a future PR, could be nice to do this for extension style traits (e.g., `AppAssetExt` etc.) so the preludes aren't so heavy with names.

_Originally posted by @bushrat011899 in https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/16163#discussion_r1821705357_
comments:
This is a duplicate of https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/13959 btw :)

Although this issue does seem to go further and say that `use trait as _` should be preferred even if it's not being re-exported (not just `pub use trait as _`). I'd personally agree with that as well, although that's more of a question of style.
Closed in favor of the other issue
